# Publishing the docs site (deployment runbook)

How to take this repo's `docs/` folder live as a public documentation site,
while keeping the GitHub fork **private**. The published site is public even
when the repo is private — that is the normal setup.

This is an internal ops doc; it is not part of the published site.

## What you'll end up with

- Source: your private fork `github.com/bconsolvo/RyzenAI-SW`, docs in `/docs`.
- A public site at a free `https://<project>.mintlify.app` URL (no custom domain needed).
- Auto-deploy on every push to `main`; preview builds + checks on every PR.

## Prerequisites

- You are an admin/owner of the fork (you are — it's under your account).
- `docs/docs.json` exists (it does) and the site builds locally: `cd docs && npx mint dev`.

## Step 1 - Create the Mintlify project

1. Go to https://mintlify.com/start and sign up / log in.
2. When prompted to connect a Git provider, choose **GitHub** and authorize.
3. Choose **Connect an existing repository** (not "let Mintlify create one").

## Step 2 - Install the GitHub App on your fork

This is the "add a GitHub" UI you saw — it's the **Mintlify GitHub App**, the
piece that lets Mintlify read the repo and rebuild on push. It works with
**private** repos.

1. In the connect flow (or later under **Dashboard → Settings → Git Settings**),
   click to install the GitHub App.
2. GitHub will ask which account/repos to grant. Select **only**
   `bconsolvo/RyzenAI-SW` (you can scope the app to a single repo).
3. Approve. You must have admin on the repo to install it (you do).

## Step 3 - Point Mintlify at the `/docs` subfolder (important)

Our `docs.json` is in `docs/`, not the repo root, so tell Mintlify where to look:

1. Dashboard → **Git Settings**.
2. Select the repository `bconsolvo/RyzenAI-SW` and the branch `main`.
3. Enable the **Set up as monorepo** toggle.
4. Enter the documentation path: `/docs` (no trailing slash).
5. **Save changes.**

If you skip this, Mintlify looks for `docs.json` at the repo root and the build fails.

## Step 4 - Get your public URL

- After the first deploy, the **Overview** page of the dashboard shows your URL,
  e.g. `https://ryzen-ai-xxxx.mintlify.app`. That's the public site — share it freely.
- The repo can stay private; the site is still publicly reachable.

## Step 5 - Day-to-day publishing

- Push (or merge a PR) to `main` → Mintlify rebuilds and deploys automatically.
- Every PR gets a **preview deployment** and runs Mintlify's checks (broken
  links, etc.) before merge. These complement the repo's own CI in
  `.github/workflows/`.
- If a change doesn't appear: Dashboard → Overview → **trigger a deployment**,
  and confirm the GitHub App is still installed on the repo.

## Already configured in the repo (no dashboard action needed)

- **GitHub + Discord links** in the sidebar/top-left are set in `docs/docs.json`
  (`navigation.global.anchors`): GitHub → `amd/RyzenAI-SW`, Discord →
  `https://discord.gg/amd-dev`. Change them there, not in the dashboard.
- **Sidebar icons**, navigation, theme, and the AI "Ask/Copy" menu are all in
  `docs/docs.json`.

## "View as Markdown" / Ask-AI 404s locally — expected

The contextual menu ("Copy page", "View as Markdown", "Open in ChatGPT/Claude")
and the Markdown export routes (`/page.md`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`) are
generated by Mintlify's **hosted** build. They are **not served by `mint dev`**,
so on `localhost:3000` those links return 404. This is expected — they start
working as soon as the site is deployed (Step 5) or on a PR preview build.
Nothing to change in `docs.json`.

## Notes / gotchas

- **Private repo limitation:** Mintlify's "edit suggestions" and "raise issue"
  reader buttons only work on **public** repos, so they'll be disabled while the
  fork is private. Everything else (public site, search, AI assistant,
  auto-deploy) works normally.
- **Custom domain (optional, later):** Dashboard → Custom domain setup → add
  `docs.yourdomain.com` → add the shown `CNAME` (to `cname.mintlify.builders`)
  at your DNS provider. Not needed if you're happy with the `*.mintlify.app` URL.
- **Plan:** the PR CI checks and some features may require a paid plan; the free
  tier covers a public site on the `*.mintlify.app` domain with auto-deploy.
